Read a selected passage

The beginning

Preface · opening excerpt

It began with a sermon.

I didn't intend to write this book.

I intended to preach a single sermon.

One sermon. One Sunday. One warning about technology, identity, and the rise of artificial intelligence. One word for a people who feel the ground shifting beneath their feet: who sense the world accelerating faster than their souls can process.

But as I opened Scripture... As I prayed... As I studied... As I listened... As I watched what is unfolding in our world...

I realized this wasn't just a sermon.

It was a story.

A story stretching from Eden to algorithm. From the first breath to the last scroll. From the garden where God asked "Where are you?" to the screen asking "Who are you?" A story written in the language of image, identity, worship, and formation. A story whispered by prophets, embodied by Jesus, and finalized in Revelation.

A story every human is already living, even if they don't realize it.

Not fear. Formation.

Chapter 9 · Selah · book p. 163

A moment to breathe.

Fear is not the point.

I didn't write this book to make you scared of your phone. I didn't lay out the seed war so you could side-eye every piece of technology like it's a demon. I didn't explain the beast system so you could start hoarding canned goods and building a bunker in Montana.

If you finish this book more afraid than when you started, I failed.

The goal is not fear. The goal is formation. The goal is awareness. The goal is that you would see clearly, stand firmly, and live faithfully, not cowering in a corner, but walking in authority.

Because here's what you need to remember:

You're not the general. You're not the one who has to win this war. You're not carrying the weight of human history on your shoulders.

You're a child.

A child of the King who already won.

Life at home

Chapter 10 · book pp. 175–176 · selected practices

A family Rule of Life.

What does a family structured for formation actually look like? Here are eight components:

1. Scripture at the Table

Read the Bible together as a family. It doesn't have to be long or elaborate. Five minutes at dinner. A verse at breakfast. Something that makes God's Word a normal, daily presence.

2. Prayer Rhythm

Pray together. Morning. Evening. Before meals. When crises hit. When joys come. Make prayer the default response to life.

…

5. Digital Discipleship Conversations

Talk about what's happening online. Ask questions. Share your own struggles. Make the digital world a topic of ongoing conversation, not a forbidden zone.

6. Family Sabbath

Take a day each week to rest, disconnect, and be present with each other and with God. Model what it looks like to not be enslaved to devices.

A different rhythm

Chapter 14 · Daily Practices · book p. 223

Before the screen.

1. Morning Liturgy (Before the Screen)

The first hour of your day sets the trajectory. If the algorithm gets you first, it shapes your imagination before God speaks.

Before you check email, before you scroll, before you consume, pray. Read Scripture. Be still. Let God speak first.

2. Scripture as Bread

Just as your body needs daily food, your soul needs daily Word.

Not as duty. As nourishment. As the voice that tells you what's true when everything else lies.

3. Prayer Throughout

Not just morning and evening, but throughout the day. Brother Lawrence called it "practicing the presence of God."

Pray while you drive. Pray while you work. Pray while you wait. Turn every margin into an altar.

4. Evening Examen

Before sleep, review the day. Where did you see God? Where did you resist Him? What are you grateful for? What do you need to confess?

This practice (developed by Ignatius of Loyola) helps you pay attention to your formation. It surfaces patterns you might otherwise miss.

05 / BEHIND THE BOOK

THEOLOGY. TECHNOLOGY. FORMATION.
“I didn’t intend to write this book.

JB✦

Jonathan C. Bilima

Jonathan’s work sits at the intersection of theology, technology, and cultural analysis. He writes to help people see the biblical story with fresh eyes—and live it with courage.

This book carries the questions of a teacher and a father: what is shaping us, and how do we form a generation that can stand?

Groups & speaking inquiries ↗

Before you
turn the page.

Is this a book against technology?+

No. The book contrasts tools that serve God’s purposes with tools that substitute for relationship and presence. Its question is what your tools are forming—and whose purposes they serve.

Does it explore prophecy and the end times?+

Yes. It engages Genesis, Daniel, and Revelation, while explicitly rejecting date-setting and rapture timelines. Its emphasis is spiritual formation, faithful readiness, and hope in Jesus.

Can we read it with a church or small group?+

Yes. Appendix A includes discussion questions around the introduction and Chapters 1–14. For group copies or speaking inquiries, contact hello@jonathanbilima.com.

Where can I see editions, price, and delivery?+

Visit the Amazon listing for the current formats, pricing, and delivery options. The purchase buttons take you to the author’s supplied Amazon link.
